verdict.rationale: Claude Code supports event-triggered automation via Hooks (shell commands run before/after actions like auto-format on edit or lint before commit) and via MCP server channels that push external events (Telegram, Discord, webhooks) into a session, plus scheduled/cron-style automation for recurring tasks. This covers the core of 'rules that trigger actions on events' but is spread across separate mechanisms (hooks, MCP channels, scheduling) rather than a unified rules engine, and there's no independent/community verification of hooks reliability in production. Missing for 10: a single unified rule-definition UI/spec, broader documented event types beyond pre/post tool-call and webhook messages, and hands-on/independent confirmation of hook reliability.
